To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nonlinear response of elasto-visco-plastic fluids can be described and prescribed by a combination of the following: (i) the stress-controlled framework of LAOStress, (ii) a descriptive characterization of the nonlinear rheological behavior, and (iii) a constitutive model based on the concept of strain decomposition.
the nonlinear behavior of elasto–viscoplastic fluids can be captured in a compact and physically intuitive manner by a constitutive model based on the concept of strain decomposition.

the nonlinear rheology under large amplitude oscillatory stress of a model yield stress fluid can be described and prescribed using a stress-based framework that allows for an intuitive interpretation of the constitutive behavior of these materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and use of a stress-controlled LAOS methodology to characterize nonlinear rheology, and the use of this methodology to construct and evaluate constitutive models for a Carbopol microgel.
the characterization and modeling of elasto-visco-plastic fluids using large amplitude stress-controlled oscillatory shear stress measurements.

the development and application of a stress-controlled framework to probe the nonlinear constitutive response of a yield stress fluid, which in turn leads to the development of a constitutive model that can be used to predict its rheological behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the constitutive model that incorporates the concept of strain decomposition with the concept of kinematics hardening is the simplest constitutive model that is capable of capturing the full nonlinear rheological behavior of Carbopol.
stress-controlled LAOStress is a powerful tool for probing the nonlinear rheological properties of elasto-visco-plastic materials and for developing constitutive models to describe these properties.
the nonlinear rheological behavior of the Carbopol gel can be captured in its entirety by the constitutive framework proposed here.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a new framework for characterizing the nonlinear rheology under LAOS stress control and developed constitutive models for the Carbopol microgels that are based on this new framework.

we have shown that a stress-controlled approach to nonlinear rheology is advantageous in that it provides a physically intuitive description of the nonlinear rheological behavior of a model elasti-viscoplastic material.
the stress-controlled LAOS methodology provides a simple and physically intuitive way to characterize and prescribe the nonlinear response of elasto-visco-plastic materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nonlinear response of elasto-visco-plastic materials can be accurately described using a stress-controlled constitutive model.
stress-controlled nonlinear rheology can be used to characterize the constitutive behavior of elasto- viscoplastic materials in a manner that is physically intuitive.

the nonlinear measures developed here, which are based solely on stress-controlled LAOS data, are able to capture the important features of a material’s nonlinear rheological behavior in a physically intuitive manner.
